items.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
items.summary: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. items.title: Extreme cold preserves passion fruit's vitamin C, but not all of its antioxidants
items.summary: Passion fruit can travel thousands of kilometers before it reaches international markets. Along the way, one of the food industry's biggest challenges is making sure its nutritional qualities survive processing, storage and transport.

items.title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified
items.summary: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls.

items.title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing
items.summary: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression.

items.title: Gut microbiomes of endangered primates reveal hidden toll of habitat loss
items.summary: As rainforests around the world are cleared for agriculture, livestock grazing, timber harvesting and development, habitat loss is pushing an increasing number of species toward extinction.

items.title: Rapid-scan satellite data offer clues to typhoon intensity
items.summary: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage.
